title: Fix the orders service and release 1.5.1 without downtime

ticket.subject: orders-api: 503s since Friday, and today's release must not drop traffic
body: Two things on `orders-api`, whose manifests are in `k8s/` (the cluster runs them as they are now):
1. **Since Friday's label cleanup, every call gets a 503.** The pods look fine, but the `orders-api` Service
sends traffic nowhere. It must reach all three pods again.
2. **Release 1.5.1 today, with zero downtime.** The last release (1.4.0, strategy Recreate) took the API down for
about half a minute. During today's rollout, three pods must answer traffic at every moment. Don't ship 1.5.0:
it crashes at start-up (a missing dependency); 1.5.1 fixes it.
The app needs about 20 seconds after start before it answers; it serves `GET /health` on its container port 8000
(named `http`). The files in `k8s/` are the source of truth: what runs must be what they say, so no
`kubectl set image` or `kubectl edit` behind their back.
This is the lab's simulated cluster: nothing is deployed, and your manifests are read, never executed.

acceptance.text: The orders-api Service selects the three pods and traffic reaches the app.

The manifest does not say what the cluster runs.

hints: `kubectl get endpoints orders-api` shows whom the Service sends traffic to, and `kubectl get pods --show-labels` the labels of the pods. A Service's selector must match the pod template's labels exactly.

Without a readiness probe, Kubernetes counts a pod as ready as soon as its container starts, 20 seconds before the app answers. A `readinessProbe` with `httpGet` on `/health` and `port: http` fixes that.
`strategy: RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1` adds one new pod, waits until it is ready, then removes one old pod.
Apply everything with `kubectl apply -f k8s/`, follow with `kubectl rollout status deployment/orders-api`. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/orders-api` goes back if a release goes wrong.
`kubectl describe pod NAME` and `kubectl logs NAME` explain a pod that is not ready or crashes.
